text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- WTO CONFERENCE OPENS WITH A TIMID BRAZIL
The World Trade Organization opened on Monday in Singapore, with a timid Brazil reminding delegates of the importance of the Mercosur customs union and the need to adhere to WTO rules in auto trade.
-- RUDOLPH HOHN TO LEAVE IBM BRASIL

After 10 years at the helm, Rudoplh Hohn, 56, will step down as president of IBM Brasil at the end of December, the result of a company-wide reorganization that limits the autonomy of local units and centralizes IBM's decision-making for Latin America.
-- BRAZILIAN GOVERNMENT OMITS BUDGET RECEIPTS

Brazil's government and lawmakers are in open dispute over 1.65 billion reais in revenues included in a 1997 spending plan prepared by Congress' joint budget committee but removed by government officials.
O GLOBO
-- BRAZIL'S TAX AGENCY LIMITS 1996 INCOME TAX DEDUCTIONS
Brazil's Internal Revenue Service has scrapped a series of deductions and tax abatements from the income tax for this year.
-- SANTA CLAUS WAS GOING TO DISTRIBUTE MARIJUANA IN RIO

Drug traffickers in Rio de Janeiro had gotten into the holiday spirit by preparing the perfect stocking-stuffer for your household pothead - 35 bags of marijuana decorated with Santa dolls- before being busted by police.
-- FOLK-HERO CRIMINAL DIES IN PRISON, SHOT SEVEN TIMES
The thief and kidnapper Leonardo Rodrigues Pareja, 22, reknown for giving on-the-run interviews and mocking police attempts to catch him, was shot to death in prison by fellow inmates.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- HALF OF MUNICIPALITIES LATE PAYING YEAR-END EXTRA WAGE
At least 2,500 of Brazil's 5,507 municipalities will be late in paying employees the legally required 13th-month wage, according to a congressional study.
-- PPB PARTY SAYS GOV'T TO USE DEBTORS LIST TO TWIST ARMS

The right-wing PPB party has charged Brazil's government of aims to use a Banco do Brasil list of indebted party members to force the lawmakers to vote for a bill to allow President Fernando Henrique Cardoso to stand for re-election in 1998.
-- BRAZILIAN EXPORTS ROSE THE LEAST
Brazil's exports rose the least of any other country in 1995, but it was second in rising imports, according to a report by the World Trade Organization.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- James Craig, Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 232 4411
